stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: The frame is a closed rectangular loop with four empty slots. Drag components from the right palette onto the slots. To remove a component, drag it out of its slot and drop it anywhere off-loop. Click the switch to open/close it. Advance once you've lit the lamp AND experienced at least one broken configuration.
stages.concept: A circuit lights when there is a closed loop that includes a source (battery) and a receiver (lamp). Break any point in the loop and the current stops. The switch is a make/break in that loop.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Build a proper circuit — one battery, one switch, one lamp, and one wire, one per slot — then verify that closing the switch lights the lamp and opening it turns it off. Both conditions must be observed.
stages.concept: The switch is a controlled break. Open switch = broken loop = no current. Closed switch = intact loop = current flows and the lamp lights.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Three slots are pre-filled. The lamp won't light because one slot is empty. Drag the wire into the empty slot to close the loop. Peek reveals a ghost of the answer for 1.5 s.
stages.concept: A wire is a zero-resistance conductor — the missing piece needed to complete the loop. Even a single break kills the whole current.

labels.diag_no_battery: no battery — nothing to drive current
labels.diag_no_lamp: loop is closed, but no lamp on it
labels.diag_switch_open: switch is open — click it to close
labels.tip1: drag from the palette; drag a placed component out to remove it; click the switch to toggle
labels.tip2: use exactly one of each component, then toggle the switch
labels.tip3: one slot is empty — drop the wire in

1.1: Try dragging one component onto any slot. Then drag another. See what happens.
1.2: A full loop needs 4 things in the 4 slots — including a battery.
1.3: Once lit, drag one of the placed components off-loop to see the lamp die.

2.1: Use one of each: battery, switch, lamp, wire — order doesn't matter.
2.2: Click the switch on the canvas to toggle it open/closed.
2.3: You must witness BOTH: lamp on with switch closed, AND lamp off with switch open.

3.1: Look at the four slots — one is missing a component.
3.2: The switch is already closed. What's needed to bridge the gap?
3.3: Drop the wire into the empty (right) slot.
